items.prompt: In a media metadata system, a media catalog must serve metadata for an asset. the read path may tolerate bounded freshness but must expose missing data honestly The design review focuses on abuse, fraud, spam, ddos, and rate-control design. constraints: the read path may tolerate bounded freshness but must expose missing data honestly
Choose the mechanism that directly satisfies the stated contract before adding adjacent controls.
The primary decision is apply layered abuse controls with identity, cost, fairness, and escalation signals..
Keep the scenario provider-neutral and do not rely on a canonical product solution.

options.text: Apply layered abuse controls with identity, cost, fairness, and escalation signals. In this normal path for media metadata, rate limits are only one control; abuse prevention must protect both the system and legitimate users. The owner must also make a lagging derived projection observable rather than silently passing it to another layer.
Choose the nearest familiar component and let each caller decide abuse, fraud, spam, ddos, and rate-control design independently, without a shared owner or failure contract.
Add replication, caching, retries, or asynchronous buffering immediately, even though the scenario has not shown that mechanism is the limiting constraint.
Keep the happy path and treat a lagging derived projection as an operational exception that the caller can resolve manually.
Select a named cloud or vendor product first and infer the workload, ownership, and guarantee from that product's defaults.

feedback.Reason: Apply layered abuse controls with identity, cost, fairness, and escalation signals. It addresses the read path may tolerate bounded freshness but must expose missing data honestly through an explicit mechanism and keeps a lagging derived projection inside a visible ownership and recovery boundary.
